name: settings_dark_100
textInBuiltTree: These are planning preferences, not scientific laws. The defaults are common rules of thumb; adjust them to your sky, your targets and your rig.
Changes when the planner counts time as usable.
Below this the target is not counted as usable. Low altitude means more atmosphere, extinction and poor seeing.
−18° is full astronomical darkness. −15° or −12° give longer windows with a brighter sky background.
Off: the Moon never excludes time.
Off: the forecast never excludes time.
Changes the capture budget and the fit verdict.
A plan that leaves less than this share of the available time free is marked "tight".

From the end of one frame to the start of the next: the download or processing, plus any delay you set. A camera timer counted start to start gives its interval minus the exposure. Settling after a dither is the Dither overhead, not this. An assumption — measure your rig.
